newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ICTSI eyes more foreign ports.
newsitem.headline: ICTSI eyes more foreign ports.

text.p: Port operator International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) is looking at investing in more foreign ports after its two existing ones have proved to be profitable, ICTSI officials said on Monday.
Aside from container port handling, the company would also diversify its services to break bulk and grains terminal operations, chief finance officer Roberto Jayme told analysts.
"We're trying to expand our wings into non-container operations," Jayme said.

"Container terminals are still more profitable than non-container terminals. However, the market niche that we are addressing have a lot of bulk and break bulk terminals, which we don't want to count ourselves out of just because we are a container terminal operator," he added.
Among its biggest prospects is the bidding for the Santos port in Brazil, the biggest port in the south American country, which is scheduled in August.
The company is also setting its sights on a terminal in Argentina, Jayme added.
"There is a grains terminal in Rosario in Argentina which we're looking at and might get involved in," he said.

The port operator, which currently operates the Manila international container port in the Philippines, Veracruz port in Mexico and the Puerto Nuevo port in Argentina, recently won 20-year operating rights to Ensenada port in Mexico's Pacific coast.
Aside from the container terminal, the company is also looking at building a cruise terminal. "It looks very promising, but nothing is definite about that yet," Jayme said.
A joint venture firm in Veracruz would also be investing in a grains terminal, just beside the Ensenada port.

Jayme also said the company was bidding for the operation of Dammam port in Saudi Arabia by the end of the month. The port, which has the capacity to handle up to 300,000 TEU annually, has set a floor for the bids at 10 million dollars.
President Rogelio Salazar said ICTSI's overseas operations had performed exceptionally well in the first four months of the year.
Cargo volume rose by 35 percent in the Buenos Aires port, while 50 percent growth was registered in its Veracruz port.
The Karachi port is expected to be in operation in about 18 months.
